newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef traded higher on mostly moderate demand and offerings during the holiday week, according to USDA.

Reduced slaughter and fairly strong immediate retail demand helped stimulate the cutout to its higher level. However, future needs were rather light as retailers look at alternate protein sources after months of beef featuring.

Rib and round cuts were steady to firm with the most advances in the light Choice rib cuts and the Select round cuts. Chuck cuts regained all of last week's loses and traded higher for the week on fairly good seasonal demand. Loin cuts trended higher throughout the week.
Closely trimmed trade was mixed as chuck cuts traded sharply higher, while the round and loin cuts were generally steady. Beef trimmings were firm on light to moderate demand and offerings.
Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were sharply lower on fairly light post holiday demand and moderate offerings; however, increased demand was noted at week's end at the lower price levels.

For the week: Select and Choice rib primal steady to 3.00 higher; Select and Choice chuck primal 1.00 to 3.00 higher; Select and Choice round primal steady to 2.00 higher; Select and Choice loin primal 1.00 to 2.50 higher; Closely trimmed items 1.00 to 1.50 higher; Beef trimmings 2.00 higher; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items 4.00 to 7.00 lower.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 1.27 at 103.63; 700/850 Up 1.81 at 102.56; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up .86 at 99.24; 700/850 Up 1.35 at 98.28.

COW AND BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT Slaughter cow receipts were moderate across many areas of the country, at mostly steady to weak live prices. The boneless beef market remained lower this week on continued seasonal light demand.

Increased supplies and a declining boneless market pressured the cow carcasses market lower. Moreover, cow cuts traded generally steady on light to moderate demand and offerings. Utility carcasses 1.00 lower; Cutter 1.00-2.00 lower. Fresh 90% boneless beef 1.00 lower; 85% 1.00-2.00 lower; 75% steady to 2.00 lower; 65% weak to 1.00 lower.
The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, September 5, 1996 was estimated at 69.03 per cwt., down 0.71 from a week ago Friday.
